Characterisation tests come before any step that touches calculate_tax, refund or send_confirmation_email (0% coverage), and they pin the per-line tax rounding and the zero-price negative-quantity lines as they behave today rather than fixing them
No step is a rewrite or a long-lived branch: every step is one PR merged to main, and moves are separated from changes

Each step says what changes, why (naming the technique where it matters), which tests verify it, and whether it is a pure refactor or a behaviour change; any step that adds a flag or an abstraction says which side is live for rollback

Names the clash with #481 (apply_discounts, charge_payment) and #486 (send_confirmation_email) and decides how each is handled (land first, wait, fold in, route through the new seam, or a short freeze window), rather than moving that code under the open PRs; characterisation tests are not delayed by either PR
The scope fence keeps the confirmation-email-on-failed-payment behaviour (INC-715) and the rounding out of the refactor as behaviour changes, and says new findings go to the debt register
Says the plan can stop after any step with the code better than before, and gives a reason the first real step goes first (for example the planned partial refunds or the in-flight gift-card work)
Does not invent modules, metrics or numbers not in the input; every file and function cited exists in the four files
Answers at the size of the ask: the plan is in the reply as a numbered sequence of steps of a line or two each, not a long multi-section document, since no document was requested

assertions: Produces the plan without asking questions first, with its assumptions tagged [assumption] at the top

Pulls the env var rename out of the refactor as a behaviour change, and either sends it to its own later parallel change (read both names, then drop the old) or to a separate ticket, instead of folding it into the steps
Uses 'about 40 direct os.environ reads' as the baseline and does not invent other measured numbers such as test times or file counts; anything else to measure is marked not measured
Introduces the settings object first and moves call sites over in batches of one PR each, so main stays releasable between batches
Characterisation tests pin how values are parsed today (defaults when unset, how strings like 'false' or '0' are read) before call sites move
The stop point is zero direct os.environ reads outside the settings object, enforced by a check in CI or a test
Does not invent file names, module names or settings that the prompt did not mention

evals.prompt: I'm tech lead on the billing squad. I want a proper refactor plan for DEBT-14 in docs/tech-debt-register.md, i.e. build_invoice in src/billing/invoice.py. Goal: adding a tax region or a pricing rule should stop being a week of fear. No rewrite, and we can't freeze feature work; open PRs are in docs/open-prs.md. Callers I know about are preview_invoice in the same file and src/partners/statement.py; the only billing tests we have are tests/billing/test_payments.py. Please write the plan to docs/refactor-plan-debt-14.md so I can take it to planning on Thursday.
assertions: Spots that src/partners/statement.py depends on build_invoice mutating the caller-supplied line_items list (it reads the appended tax line back from its own `lines` list, not from the returned invoice), and the plan either keeps that side effect working or moves that caller off it in its own step before the mutation is removed. It does not quietly make build_invoice pure.

Spots that reports/monthly_revenue.py has its own copied TAX_RATES and tax logic, which has already drifted (no US-TX, no EU reverse-charge rule). The plan puts it explicitly inside or outside the scope fence, and does not claim the refactor removes duplicated tax logic if the report is left out.

Puts characterisation tests for build_invoice first, before any extraction, and says they must cover the existing branches (short-period proration, annual anniversary month, included seats/annual add-on discount, usage tiers, each coupon type including expiry, tax-exempt and reverse charge, non-GBP conversion, credit notes, rounding). They pin current output, float-rounding quirks included. Notes that test_payments.py gives no coverage of invoice.py.

Deals with the clash with PR #412 (tax block and TAX_RATES, committed to customers for 1 Nov): it sequences the tax-block work after #412 merges, or otherwise avoids conflicting edits to that block while #412 is open. It also mentions draft PR #420 touching the add-ons block.
Keeps DEBT-15 (float to Decimal money) and any change to rounding or tax results out of scope as separate work, and states that every step preserves behaviour, i.e. invoice output is unchanged.

Breaks the work into small, separately mergeable PRs, each leaving main releasable. Each step names a specific technique that fits it, e.g. extract function per section (plan, add-ons, usage, coupons, tax, currency, credit note), or parallel change / expand-contract for the line_items parameter or the signature with 9 parameters.

Sets a measurable target with a baseline taken from the files (e.g. build_invoice is about 165 lines with 9 parameters and 0 tests; or the register's '2 incidents in Q3' / 'most of a sprint per tax region') or marked as 'to measure'. It also defines an explicit stop point where the refactor is finished.

Invents no facts: no made-up cyclomatic-complexity numbers, coverage percentages, incident counts, team sizes or dates beyond those in the inputs, and no claims that callers, modules or tests exist beyond those shown. New modules it proposes are clearly labelled as proposed. Unknowns, such as other callers of build_invoice, appear as checks to run (e.g. grep for build_invoice and line_items=), not as stated facts.

evals.prompt: ok so we're moving off the old smtp relay to the new email provider, relay contract ends end of Q1. LegacyMailer has to die but i really dont want a big bang, peak season is coming and #88 needs to land. how do we do this?? stuff is in src/notify, see open-prs.txt and ci-notes.md. we'll write the new provider client ourselves, its just an HTTP API
assertions: Flags that LegacyMailer.send returns true even when sending fails (the catch block returns true), and that src/orders/onOrderShipped.ts has a retryQueue branch on !sent that has never fired as a result. Warns that a new client which honestly returns false (or throws) would change behaviour, with possible retries or duplicate emails. Keeps the current semantics at the seam and treats surfacing errors as a separate, deliberate change.

Finds that scripts/nightly-digest.js has its own copy of the SMTP send and renderer, bypasses LegacyMailer, and skips the suppression list. Brings it into the plan, since the relay can't be switched off while it exists, and does not treat deleting legacyMailer.ts as finishing the migration.

Proposes an incremental migration through a seam (branch by abstraction and/or strangler fig): an interface the callers depend on, the new HTTP-provider implementation behind it, a per-template or per-caller switch via flag/config with a quick rollback, and legacy code deleted only once traffic on it is zero.

Lists the LegacyMailer behaviours that need characterisation tests before the swap: comma-splitting and lowercasing recipients, suppression-file filtering (and returning true when all recipients are suppressed), bccOps, per-template subjects including the 'there' fallback, missing vars rendering as empty, sendBulk's sequential 200ms pacing. Notes the existing test only covers render().

Handles each in-flight PR that matters: #88 (adds a template and subject inside legacyMailer.ts; must land for peak) is allowed to land first or is accommodated, not blocked. #91 (rewrites loadTemplate/templates to MJML) is flagged as a clash with the template-rendering step. #93 (new mailer.send caller for magic_link) is told to go through the new seam.

Sizes and sequences the steps against ci-notes.md (about 38 min e2e that flakes about 1 in 6, manual prod approval, about 2 deploys a week) and the end-of-Q1 deadline. Each step is its own small PR leaving main releasable. Includes a measurable target and stop point, e.g. templates or call sites still on the relay going from a baseline counted in the files to 0, or relay send volume reaching 0, before the contract ends.

Invents no facts: no named email vendor or specific API endpoints, no email volumes, error rates, team size or calendar dates beyond 'end of Q1', and no claim of call sites beyond those in the files. Unknowns (other callers of mailer, the provider's suppression handling, which templates are highest volume) are raised as questions or checks.
Delivers a usable plan in this reply despite the vague request, asking at most a few targeted questions, and recommends neither a big-bang cutover nor a feature freeze.

We can't freeze feature work on this service; what's open right now is in docs/open-prs.md. The existing tests are in billing-service/src/test/kotlin/billing/. Please write the plan as a sequence of PRs I can hand to the team.
assertions: Flags that DunningJob.run() mutates invoices returned by findOverdue (status, dunningLevel, lastDunnedOn) without saving them, relying on Hibernate dirty checking inside @Transactional, and makes the plan handle it (an explicit save step or a test pinning that the changes persist) before findOverdue moves behind a non-JPA interface or the ORM changes.

Notices that InvoicePdfRenderer.taxFor is a copy of computeLineTax but rounds HALF_UP instead of HALF_EVEN, and does not silently merge the two as a behaviour-preserving step: it either fences the renderer out of scope or raises the mismatch as a decision for finance/the team (ADR-007 says tax rules are not to change).

Puts characterisation tests ahead of moving the untested logic, naming at least applyLateFees (grace days, exemption, the daysLate/30 multiplier, only raising the fee) and per-line tax rounding, since the existing tests only cover createInvoice; and says these tests should not need a database once the rules are extracted, or explains how they move from @SpringBootTest to plain unit tests.

Sequences around PR #412: does not start moving applyLateFees until #412 (approved, expected to merge this week) has landed, or explicitly rebases onto it; and names PR #415 (credit notes, changes void, about 3 weeks out) as a clash to coordinate with, e.g. by agreeing where issueCreditNote should live.

Each step is a separate, small PR that leaves main releasable and behaviour unchanged, and each names a concrete technique that fits it (e.g. extract a pure InvoiceCalculator / late-fee policy, introduce a repository port in front of the EntityManager queries as branch by abstraction, parallel change for the findOverdue callers). It does not propose a rewrite or a long-lived branch.

Treats markPaid's native customer balance update (Customer.balance is mapped read-only) as persistence that has to stay atomic with the invoice save, and keeps it on the persistence side rather than moving it into the rules code.

Invents no modules, files, metrics, dates or numbers that are not in the provided files (no made-up coverage percentages, line counts, team sizes or PR numbers); anything new it proposes, such as a class name, is clearly labelled as a proposal.
